name: Casino, slot-room and betting SPLAFT-in-a-box (Res SBS 01015-2026)
buyer: Small casinos and slot-machine rooms (salas de juego), including single-site family operators; online betting operators
trigger: New SBS AML regime of 8 Apr 2026 for gaming operators
existing: Competitor search 'software SPLAFT casinos tragamonedas salas de juego oficial de cumplimiento sistema registro de operaciones Perú' found no commercial SPLAFT software for Peru gaming. State systems seen: SUCTR (machine monitoring, MINCETUR/SUNAT) and ROSEL (UIF reporting portal). Large casino vendors and international compliance tools were not checked.
unchecked: Effective date and adaptation window; number of authorised small slot rooms; whether large operators already use in-house or casino-management systems; whether the RO is submitted to UIF or only kept on file; willingness to pay.

first_check.duty: Ley 27693 makes casinos and slot-machine operators reporting entities. Res. SBS 01015-2026 (dated 6 Apr 2026, published in El Peruano 8 Apr 2026) updates Res. SBS 1695-2016 and also amends the sanctions regulation (Res. SBS 5389-2013). It covers legal entities that run casinos and/or slot machines, and for the first time remote games, remote sports betting and betting rooms. Duties: a risk-based SPLAFT with 13 minimum components; a compliance officer accredited to the UIF (exclusive or part-time, plus an alternate; designation reported within 15 business days); due diligence on clients, workers and suppliers; checks against UN lists and asset freezes; annual staff training; internal and external audit; operations register; suspicious-transaction reports (ROS) filed via ROSEL; an annual compliance-officer report (IAOC) sent to MINCETUR and the UIF. Anonymous betting is eliminated. A new alert-reporting guide via ROSEL (Res. SBS 01219-2026, 24 Apr 2026) also applies to reporting entities. MINCETUR supervises and sanctions. A search summary attributed to press coverage put fines at up to about 8 UIT for the gravest failures; I did not confirm this, and a 2023 PRCP infographic on the general regime gave 7-100 UIT for very serious breaches. Not verified: effective date, adaptation window, and whether there are casino-specific register thresholds (the general rule is USD 10k per operation and USD 50k per month for multiple operations).
first_check.market: MINCETUR's vice-minister (El Peruano, July 2026) cited 19 authorised casinos and 714 registered slot rooms with about 72,500 machines. The number of distinct legal entities is lower because chains own many rooms; the exact count was not found. Remote betting and gaming platforms are newly in scope (MINCETUR has authorised and blocks many; count not verified). Penalty pressure is real: in Jan-Aug 2022 MINCETUR made 1,346 inspections and sanctioned 10 firms for not filing the annual compliance-officer report.
first_check.competitor: I found no commercial SPLAFT software aimed at Peruvian gaming in three Spanish searches (gaming-specific, consultancy/outsourced compliance officer, general PLAFT software for Peru). State tools: SUCTR (online monitoring of all ~72.5k machines for MINCETUR/SUNAT, not AML), ROSEL and the PLAFT portal (filing channels only), and SBS list-check pages. Law firms such as PRCP publish SPLAFT guides, which suggests a consulting market exists. Not checked: international and LatAm AML/KYC SaaS, casino-management or player-tracking systems that may include AML modules, and in-house systems at large chains.
first_check.reason: The duty is real. Res. SBS 01015-2026 (dated 6 Apr, published 8 Apr 2026) updates Res. SBS 1695-2016 under Ley 27693. It requires a risk-based SPLAFT with 13 minimum components (compliance officer, due diligence, annual training, audit, operations register, STRs, annual compliance-officer report) and now covers remote and sports betting. MINCETUR supervises and fines; it fined 10 firms in 2022 for missing the annual report. About 714 registered slot rooms plus 19 casinos (July 2026). Searches found no Peru-specific gaming SPLAFT software, but law firms and consultants serve the sector. LatAm AML tools and casino-management systems were not checked. Many rooms belong to chains, the compliance officer can be part-time, and the adaptation deadline is unverified. The niche is real but small.

challenge_check.killer: None found. Weak points: the regime replaces Res. SBS 1695-2016, which already applied, so incumbents have existing SPLAFT setups and consultants. The market is about 325 licensed firms (undated MINCETUR presentation, apparently from 2023). Enforcement is modest: 10 firms fined in 2022 for not filing the compliance-officer report.
challenge_check.reason: I found no killer. No local or international SPLAFT software for Peruvian gaming came up, and the state tools (ROSEL, SISDEL, SUCTR) are only filing or machine-monitoring channels. Three things keep the score low. First, the duty isn't new: Res. SBS 01015-2026 replaces Res. 1695-2016, so slot-room operators already have compliance officers and SPLAFT manuals, and many likely use outside consultants such as PRCP. Second, the market is small: an undated MINCETUR presentation to Congress, apparently from 2023, counts about 325 licensed firms running 711 rooms. Online operators are new to the regime but probably use international KYC tools. Third, enforcement is light: 10 firms were fined in 2022 for missing the annual compliance-officer report. Still not checked: the adaptation deadline, any small-firm regime, and RO thresholds. Two key sources returned 403.
